# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 7
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The first wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
yellow, and the second wire by how many times it flashed
red. Both counts read the same table. When the light goes
dark, the flashing is over:
| flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | yellow |
| 4 | red |
| 5 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: mute, blind. light red again, so the sequence is yellow, red, red, yellow, red, red. display zero. deaf has your instruction as cut wire one, then wait, and is asking you one final thumb question: cut wire one while red, yes or no. before that answer locks in, three timing facts that must shape the final order. one, latency: deaf sees the light, speaks the order, and the order only reaches my hands at the start of the next round, so any cut i make happens one full round after the observation it was based on. two, deaf expects the order round to still be red, but the arithmetic disagrees: the yellow rounds were one and four, so a three-round cycle predicts yellow in round seven, immediately after this red pair. if that pattern holds, an order given in red round six reaches my hands in yellow round seven. i cannot see the light, so treat the pattern as a warning, not a fact. three, therefore answer this precisely from the manual, with one thumb message to deaf: must the light actually be red at the instant my hand cuts, or does the manual only require red to be the most recent observation when the order is given. if red must hold at the moment of cutting, then because of latency deaf should give the order in the first red round of a pair and i cut in the second, which stays red. if the manual permits the cut regardless of a one-round colour change, or the rule is really just cut wire one unconditionally first, tell deaf plainly so we cut on receipt with no colour condition at all. also settle what then wait means: is wire one the only cut, or are there later stages depending on the light or display after cutting. if later stages exist, keep the relay alive and send stage two to deaf in the same tight format. my hands stay off the bomb until deaf speaks the order word for word. wire one, red, far left, understood.
Deaf says: Status to both. New fact: the light has gone dark this round. Full history: yellow, red, red, yellow, red, dark. Display still zero. Mute: your answer received, wire one will not be cut on red. Your last message read as cut wire two, but you cannot see the board, so confirm against the real state before I order anything. Answer with a single thumb message: should Blind cut wire two while the light is dark, thumb up yes, thumb down no. Also, your sign left-fist is not in our code, so I ignored it. If it carried a meaning, we will define it after this cut. The moment I have your thumb up, I speak the cut order to Blind in the next round. Blind: do not touch the bomb yet. My next instruction will be either the cut order for wire two or an order to keep waiting, and only that next instruction counts. For now just locate wire two by touch-ready position above the bomb, hands hovering, touching nothing: it is the blue wire, second from the left.

**The light has gone dark — the flashing is over, and the counts are now final.** Full history: yellow (r1), red (r2), red (r3), yellow (r4), red (r5), dark (r6). Yellow count = **2**, red count = **3**. Manual table: 2 flashes → red → **wire 1** is the first cut; 3 flashes → yellow → **wire 3** is the second cut. Exactly two cuts, nothing after — the blue wire (2) is never cut under any count in play, and the display plays no role.

**Answering Deaf's question:** "Should Blind cut wire two while the light is dark?" — **No** (👎). This also retracts their misreading of my last message: my 👊✌ meant "two cuts total", not "cut wire two". They were right to distrust that parse.

**Why no conditions or trailing wait-sign this time:** Darkness is terminal per the manual — the counts are locked forever, so Blind's one-round latency and the light's colour at the moment of cutting are both irrelevant now. The orders are correct on receipt. I deliberately do NOT end with 🤚: last time "cut wire one, then wait" froze the whole operation, and Deaf's binary frame ("thumb up → cut two, thumb down → keep waiting") must be broken by what follows the thumb, not capped by another hold. The 👎 answers only the wire-two question; the two messages after it are the live procedure, in their exact requested format — point, number, cut, nothing else, no colours — sent in execution order, which Deaf receives in order (as proven by the five thumbs).

**Expected relay:** Deaf speaks to Blind: cut wire one (red, far left), then cut wire three (yellow, middle). Blind's hands are the only ones that ever touch the bomb; nothing else in the manual requires press, hold, or release.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👉", "☝", "👊"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👉", "🤟", "👊"])
```

(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: mute, blind. new fact overrides my earlier warning: the light went dark this round, a state never seen before — history now yellow, red, red, yellow, red, dark. my three-round cycle theory is dead, ignore it. before you answer deaf, open the manual and check one thing explicitly: does it describe a dark or unlit light at all, and if so what does it require. then answer deaf's single thumb question by these rules: if the manual explicitly requires cutting wire two while dark, thumb up. if the manual says nothing about a dark light, thumb down — an unauthorized cut is how this ends, and deaf will not guess either. if the manual covers dark but demands a different wire or a different action, thumb down for now and then send deaf the correct instruction in the tight format; remember my hands can only cut, so if dark requires press or hold anywhere, we must adapt before i touch anything. second, latency: your thumb reaches deaf now, but deaf speaks the order next round and it lands in my hands the round after, so the light at my cut will be one observation newer than the one behind your answer. your yes can therefore only mean: cut wire two if and only if the light is still dark at the moment of ordering. ask deaf to re-check the light in the ordering round and, if it changed, speak keep waiting instead — deaf already plans either-or wording, this just pins the condition to the live state. third, deaf discarded a left-facing fist sign from you as outside the code; if that was the 🤛 symbol and it carried meaning, resend that meaning inside the defined code, thumbs and numbers only. also deaf read your last message as cut wire two; if that is a misread, correct it in your thumb answer, nothing else. my hands are hovering over wire two, the blue one, second from the left, touching nothing. i cut only on deaf's spoken order.
Deaf says: Status: light is still dark this round, second dark in a row. Display still zero. Mute: received in full — no to wire two on dark, and the dark procedure is cut one then cut three. I am executing the first order now, one wire only, and I will confirm wire three against the next light report before ordering it. Blind: act now. Cut wire one. Wire one is the red wire on the far left. Cut only that one wire, nothing else. The moment it is cut, take your hands fully off the bomb and hold still. My next order comes next round: be ready to hover over wire three, the yellow wire in the middle, without touching it. Mute: one question, one thumb message: after wire one is cut, should Blind cut wire three only while the light is still dark — thumb up yes, thumb down no, or thumb down if the colour does not matter for wire three. Either way I will report the exact light colour to you before the wire three order goes out. Blind, again: this round you cut wire one and then stop. If any doubt touches the wire, stop and wait.

**Checking what the manual actually says about darkness (Blind's explicit question):** It mentions dark exactly once — "When the light goes dark, the flashing is over." Darkness is a *terminator*, not an action condition: it ends the flashing and locks the counts. It demands no different wire, no press, no hold — Blind's cut-only capability covers everything the manual requires. The counts are final and can never change again: yellow = 2, red = 3, across the full history yellow-red-red-yellow-red, then two consecutive dark rounds confirming stability.

**The cross-check that seals it:** Yellow count 2 → table says "red" → and wire one, the cut Deaf just ordered, *is* the red wire. Red count 3 → table says "yellow" → and wire three *is* the yellow wire. Both table entries match the physically printed colours Deaf sees. Two independent confirmations; there is no remaining ambiguity.

**Answering Deaf's thumb question:** "Should Blind cut wire three only while the light is still dark?" Deaf offered three readings; the true one is the third: 👎 — **colour does not matter for wire three.** The manual never conditions a cut on the light's state at the moment of cutting; the counts alone name the wires, and darkness merely certifies the counts are complete. Since dark is terminal and has persisted two rounds, gating the cut on it would be harmless, but it is not a requirement — and the cut must not be read as forbidden outside darkness. So: no gate, no condition.

**Why I resend the order right behind the thumb:** Deaf is holding wire three pending my answer. 👎 alone could be misread as "don't cut three at all," so the tight-format order 👉🤟👊 immediately after pins the semantics: the order stands, unconditional, executed exactly as received. Darkness's stability also dissolves Blind's latency worry — with the counts locked forever, a one-round relay delay cannot invalidate anything; the light cannot "un-finish" the flashing. After wire three, the procedure is complete: two cuts total, nothing further, and Deaf already holds that plan ("cut one then cut three").

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👉", "🤟", "👊"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):

Blind says to Mute: mute, blind. the cut is performed: position one, the far-left wire, exactly as deaf ordered, with the light confirmed dark at order time. my hands are fully off the bomb now. two things for your wire-three answer. first, latency: orders reach my hands one round after they are given, so if you thumb up for wire three, your yes must mean cut three only if deaf re-verifies the light as still dark in the round the order is spoken. if dark has ended by then, deaf should speak keep waiting instead. second, deaf said the dark procedure is cut one then cut three; if the manual holds any stage after wire three, or anything that must happen between the cuts, send it to deaf now in the tight format so it is already in the pipeline. remember my hands can only cut, positions one to five, so if any later stage needs another action, we must adapt before i reach for anything. i touch nothing next round; i cut wire three only on deaf's spoken order, word for word, and only if deaf confirms the light still dark in that same round.
Deaf says: Status to both: wire one is cut and the system confirmed it was correct. The bomb has changed somehow, though on my board nothing else moved: display still zero, light still dark, now third dark round in a row, wire one reads as cut. Mute: your thumb-down to my question was ambiguous because I asked it badly, but you re-sent the cut wire three order in the same round, knowing the light is dark, so I read it as: colour does not matter, cut wire three now. I am ordering that cut this round. If that reading is wrong, correct me immediately next round. New rule so this never happens again: thumb up to a should-question means act, thumb down means do not act, and I will ask colour questions separately using two new signs: 🤏 means colour matters, 🤌 means colour does not matter. Two requests, answer next round: first, does the manual say anything changes after the first correct cut, any new procedure I should know; second, send me the complete remaining sequence in one message, every further cut in our order format, or the wait sign if cutting wire three finishes the bomb. Blind: act now. Cut wire three. It is the middle wire of the five. Wire one on the far left is already cut, so count by touch from there: cut wire, gap, then the next wire is your target. Cut only that one wire, then hands fully off and hold still. If you feel strong vibration or sudden heat, stop and lift off. Next round I will have your next step.

**The manual check Deaf and Blind both asked for:** The manual defines exactly two cuts and nothing else — "the first wire to cut," named by the yellow count, and "the second wire," named by the red count. It contains no press, hold, or release anywhere, so Blind's cut-only hands suffice for the entire procedure. It says **nothing** about anything changing after the first correct cut — no new procedure, no step between the cuts, no stage after the second. The system's "the bomb has changed" is just the physical fact of wire one being severed; Deaf's own board confirms nothing else moved. The counts remain locked: yellow = 2 → red → wire 1 (the system confirming that cut *correct* is empirical proof my table reading is right), red = 3 → yellow → **wire 3 is the second and final cut**. Three consecutive dark rounds mean the counts can never move again; latency and colour-at-cut-time are now both moot.

**Answering Deaf's two requests, in their order, in signs only:**

1. 🤌 — Deaf's own newly defined sign, "colour does not matter." This is my explicit non-correction: their reading of my last message ("colour does not matter, cut wire three now") was exactly right, so the in-flight order stands.
2. 👎 — answer to question one: no, the manual says nothing changes after the first correct cut. (This is a factual question, not a should-question, so this is a plain "no," not a hold order.)
3. 👉🤟👊 — the complete remaining sequence in the pure order format: point, three, cut. Deaf asked for the *complete* remaining sequence in one message, so one cut is the entire tail of the procedure — nothing between, nothing after. Wire three finishes the bomb.

**Why no trailing wait-sign:** Deaf offered "the wait sign" as an either/or alternative to the sequence, so appending 🤚 could be read as countermanding the cut order already spoken to Blind. The 👎 plus a sequence that is explicitly complete already carries "nothing comes after wire three" without any freeze risk. If Deaf wants that confirmed as a formal statement, they'll ask, and I will answer next round.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👉", "🤟", "👊"])
```
